newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dollar vols soft on stable spot, decay.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar vols soft on stable spot, decay.

text.p: Implied volatilities in dollar/pair options were soft Friday as the dollar stabilized off its peaks, and heading into the weekend.

"They're generally unchanged from this morning but from yesterday certainly they're about a quarter vol lower generally across the curve," said a trader of dollar/yen. "But it's just been quiet. Spot's been settling around, (with) generally no impetus to move things either direction."
"The vols are lower...the dollar came off the highs. The nervousness is no longer there," said another bank options trader.
"And into the weekend, of course, people start selling because they capture time decay," the second options trader added.
One-month dollar/yen was quoted at 9.65/9.9 percent near midday, down about a quarter point from Thursday but little changed from early European trade.
The one-month, 25-delta dollar/yen risk reversal held at about 0.35/0.65 point favoring yen calls.
One-month dollar/mark had slipped to 9.7/9.9 percent near midday Friday, off from about 9.9/10.1 at the New York opening but near early-European levels at 9.7/9.8 percent.
The one-month, 25-delta dollar/mark risk reversal stood at 0.3/0.6 point, favoring mark puts.
The three traders said the market had traded Friday but they cited no outstanding deals of size.
"Nothing unusual as far as size," the second trader said.
"There's really nothing going on," said the third trader. "We haven't seen much interest in options."
"We've seen some (size) but nothing specific that I can talk about," added the first broker. ((Derivatives Desk (312) 408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
